seal.statement: The learner promotion guard admits some over-target promotions on bootstrap-critical system partitions only because it re-derives a temporary overflow budget of two voters from its own priority-recovery view; the carry stage now lets the cure policy's exact-transition authorization travel with the operation, and enforcement will remove the budget. Before it can, every production path whose success can depend on that budget today must be enumerated and given one of four dispositions - explicit authority required, proved unreachable, proved obsolete, or still unclassified - and frequency of observation is never the proof: an unobserved path stays unclassified. This quest changes nothing in production. It measures the set of partitions the guard treats as bootstrap-critical and the subset the cure policy can mint for; it enumerates the budget-admitted cases by a state grid over the real count check and by a census of every producer of an add-like operation; for each case it records the path, the partition class, the triggering state, the current guard reason, the budget dependency, the semantic owner, a proposed authorization kind, the minting and validation evidence available, a reachable witness or none, and the disposition, with a precisely scoped repair quest wherever an owner would have to start minting; it audits the five mintable partitions for ways to reach the guard without the minting owner, every other admitted partition without widening the mint, and the unhealthy-source REPLACE independently of the spread cure; it inventories the whole membership-publication-epoch domain including the alias observedMembershipEpoch, reproduces reader divergence on real owners, states what makes an authorization stale and the candidate canonical models without choosing one or adding tolerance, and pins the future transition - present, correct authority, matching epoch, honoured - with its falsifiers; it settles as findings the partition-row read's timing, whether operation type is part of authority identity, and what quantity the authorized count bounds; and it proves that only the complete outcome honoured may ever replace the budget. Its output is the decision matrix, the epoch-domain inventory and the nine-point enforcement entry gate with each item's status, from which the enforce quest is later authored.

text: Sealed at metric 12 and measured the two sets plus the budget's real domain. MEASURED on the real owners at 902714be8: isBootstrapCriticalSystemPartitionId is true for all 45 system-table first partitions; authorizeSpreadCureTransition mints for exactly 5 (schema_operations, sql_transactions, sql_transaction_participants, sql_write_operations, control_plane_publications); 40 cannot. NEW and load-bearing: the guard's budget owner is not consulted outside the 6 priority-control-plane partitions at all - resolvePriorityRecoveryCompletionForLearnerPromotion returns null unless classifySystemPartition().priorityControlPlane, and its other disjunct (node readiness PRIORITY_CONTROL_PLANE_RECOVERY_PENDING) is itself only read for priorityControlPlane partitions - so temporaryOverflowVoterBudget is undefined and the cap is budget-free for the other 39, including six of the owner's seven. Exhaustive pure-owner grid over the real count check and the real completion owner: a budget-admitted row is always would_exceed_target_replica_count (the even-voter gate is never the budget's discriminator, because the budget's own precondition activeVoterCount>=target forces the cap comparison to dominate), and there are exactly four arithmetic classes (allowance in force or not, over the budget-free cap by 1 or 2). Producer census started: two createOperation callers confirmed, six add-like cure conditions from the policy's own table, and four row-writing paths that bypass createOperation.

Eight of the twelve receipts are green: partition sets, the budget-admitted grid, the add-like producer census, the mintable-five alternate routes, the unmintable-partition audit on the real guard, the unhealthy-source REPLACE, the future honoured transition with its seven falsifiers, and the only-honoured mutant falsifier. The decision matrix is written with 17 rows, 18 producers and 4 admission classes. MEASURED since the last note. The grid: 18432 rows, 3000 with a non-zero budget, 600 budget-admitted, four arithmetic classes, and the budget NEVER decides the even-voter gate. The ledger REPLACE is granted today and refused with the budget forced to 0 in a double of the completion owner; the operation-less promotion is granted at cap target+2 with no replacement allowance; every one of the 39 non-priority critical partitions decides identically with and without the budget. Routes: the mint has exactly one call site outside its own module, the at-target and ledger expand cures re-type the ADD and carry nothing, the ESTABLISHING window (planner epoch null) mints nothing while still retaining the ADD, and an undeclared partition row mints nothing. REPLACE: the three censuses reproduced on the REAL replica-inventory owner - a SYNCING row in a voter role gives activeCount 3 against activeVoterCount 4, so the suppressor passes exactly where the cap and the guard both read over target; the ordinary hand-off needs no budget, so the budget reliance is ACCIDENTAL and the hand-off over-replication is an IMPLEMENTATION ARTIFACT of promote-then-remove. Falsifiers: future epoch is HONOURED, an invalid supplied epoch reads not-evaluated, a foreign intent reads MALFORMED (so authorization_intent_unknown is unreachable from a row), and wrong-partition is caught only through the destination replica id. Carried-forward: the partition row is read once when the cure CONDITION holds even if nothing is minted, the window is fail-closed and moving the read cannot close it; the evaluation ignores the row type entirely; the authorized count bounds neither voters nor active holders but the peak of the two.

All twelve receipts green; probe metric 0. Final pass corrected three overclaims I found in my own matrix before reporting. (1) The lab count: I had written '24 of 33' from memory of the seventh addendum; re-measured with my own stated rule (a first-pass count-check line with the overflow allowance in force, not refused, and votersAfterPromotion above the budget-free cap) the three authority-carry machines carry 33 budget-dependent promotions - 29 honoured on the five (6 schema_operations, 6 sql_transactions, 6 sql_transaction_participants, 6 sql_write_operations, 5 control_plane_publications), 2 ledger REPLACE targets and 2 operation-less control_plane_publications promotions. The addendum's 37/33 came from a different rule; both numbers are now stated with their rules. (2) Admission classes per row: a producer-backed row always has an owned add-like operation at the guard, so the replacement allowance is in force and only the two allowance classes are reachable for it; only the operation-less row and the ledger row reach the no-allowance classes. Rows no longer claim classes they cannot reach. (3) The matrix, the epoch inventory and the gate markdown are now all generated from their JSON by one renderer that the validator re-runs, so the documents cannot drift from the evidence. Statics: pre-commit exit 0, duplication 57/57 src and 793/793 test groups unchanged, complexity 1816/1816 (one helper extracted to stay under it), unused exports 1438/1438 (one helper de-exported), cycles 0/0, shards regenerated and current, file-size 27/27 and 21/21, guidelines and impact-contracts pass. No file under src, examples, .github or .githooks changed.

round 1 REJECT (7 blocking). UPHELD, and it is the claim that matters most: the overflow budget can be non-zero on exactly six partitions (the five mintable ones and the operation ledger) - re-derived from code (the completion owner is consulted only when classifySystemPartition().priorityControlPlane, a pure function of the id; recoveryPending can only be true there; an undefined budget is 0) and by driving the real runLearnerPromotionCheck with the real count-check methods and completion owner against a zero-budget double over 793800 states (45 partitions x voters x learners x target x operations x six summary shapes x recoveryPending x joining x owned operation) plus 20466 odd-id states: 16320 budget-admitted states, none outside the six; the six owner-named rows and the 33-id remainder stay proved-unreachable. Also upheld: allowTemporaryOverflowPromotion is a short-circuit disjunction no src call site passes; ReplicaRecoveryService has no construction site; the lab count of 33 by the stated rule; the census disagreement on the real inventory owner; the epoch readers' divergence on real owners; no distinct raft membership epoch. B1 no matrix row for the ESTABLISHING window nor for the undeclared partition row, although the quest's own routes test proves the over-target cure ADD is retained and mints nothing in both. B2 the unhealthy-source REPLACE row rests on a false premise: unified-rebalancer-follow-up-move.js selects the REPLACE source FROM THE HEALTHY replicas, preferring a doubly-occupied node (a failed replica can never be the source) - it is a relocation off a co-located node, i.e. a spread-gap cure done by REPLACE, so the proposed kind, owner and repair scope are built on a condition no module decides; the 'end to end' test never calls the follow-up builder, planner, coordinator or guard. B3 the pinned grant rule outcome === honoured grants a promotion ABOVE the authorized bound (honoured is decided without the bound; wouldBeWithinAuthorizedBound is separate and the source says a consumer must AND them): a record authorizing 5 evaluated for a promotion to 8 is honoured; every test case sets voters equal to the bound; three wrong grant rules survive (operation mismatch, RF mismatch, intent unknown). B4 three dispositions stronger than their evidence: priority expand-for-spread ADD and paired-relocation REPLACE (no drive to the guard; budget dependence asserted, not constructed) -> still-unclassified; the operation ledger row covers 15 producers under one disposition and its lab witness is a chained REPLACE during the first one's drain, which the offered census disagreement does not explain -> split. B5 the epoch census is not complete: its pattern matches only identifiers spelling publication/membership/planning epoch - 14 uninventoried alias tokens at 19 sites found by one same-line-binding probe (source_topology_epoch, currentEpoch in the dispatch epoch gate, latestEpoch, fallbackEpoch, observedEpoch, topologyEpoch), the carrier's own tokens and the bare epoch field are absent, the limits do not disclose it, and 94 of 121 tokens leave 'which object it observes' unanswered. B6 the validator accepts wrong rows: a still-unclassified row flipped to proved-unreachable with domain 'x', the cure policy named owner of a REPLACE-bearing row, frequency language in triggering state and evidence, a domain reading 'not seen in any lab formation', the budget-dependent lab-witnessed ledger row flipped to proved-unreachable, gate items flipped to demonstrated - all green. B7 gate statuses overclaimed: item 1, 4, 7 and 8 are not-yet, item 6 is blocked-on-owner-decision (a proposed name is not a defined meaning). Non-blocking: receipt 2's one-class mapping is a tautology and the sealed wording cannot be met literally (the guard has no producer dimension) - the lead must restate it; the unreachable rows' test drives one state per partition, not the grid its domain states; the budget on one partition is switched on by ANOTHER partition's spread gap (the summary is read whole); pooled lab total instead of per-machine counts (10, 12, 11).

Lead ruling, recorded as a decision (round-2 rework). Receipt 2's sealed wording, 'every such row must map to exactly one matrix row', cannot be met literally: the guard has no producer dimension, so a budget-admitted state cannot select a producer-differentiated row, and round 1's one-class mapping was a tautology because the class was keyed on the formula that defines admission. The lead ruled the sealed wording is met as follows, and the grid test implements it: the grid maps each budget-admitted state to exactly one ADMISSION CLASS; the classes are keyed on the GUARD-VISIBLE discriminators - allowance in force, over by 1 or 2, an owned add-like operation visible or not, joining, and whether any operation is counted at all - not on the defining formula; every matrix row declares which classes it can occupy; every class is claimed by at least one row; every row claiming a class has a producer from receipt 3's census; and the classes with no owned add-like operation map to the operation-not-visible rows. MEASURED: 20 classes, re-derived by the grid test and compared with the matrix, with each discriminator asserted against the state's own inputs. Two further lead rulings are recorded in the matrix under method.leadRulings: formation evidence is reported per machine and never pooled, and the four-core machine stays a separate class that is not included in those counts.

Round-2 rework against the verifier's seven blocking findings; all twelve receipts green, probe metric 0. B1: the ESTABLISHING window and the undeclared partition row are now their OWN rows, each explicit-authority-required with a scoped unstarted repair quest, and the routes test asserts each rather than folding them into the stale-authorization row - MEASURED, the real applyOverTargetCapAddRetention RETAINS the cure ADD in both states and attaches no authorization field. B2: the unhealthy-source REPLACE row is redone from the code and renamed. MEASURED on the real owner: the source is selected FROM the healthy replicas, preferring one on a node hosting more than one, and the target is an unoccupied node; a FAILED replica is filtered out first and can never be the source. The condition is a DISTINCT-NODE SPREAD gap cured by a REPLACE - proven, as the owner asked - which makes it the same semantic the cure policy owns for ADDs, decided in a second module; the semantic owner is the follow-up move owner, the proposed kind is a new priority_recovery_relocation, and the spread-cure kind is not reused. The test now drives buildPriorityRecoveryFollowUpMove, executeMoveViaCoordinator into the real coordinator, and the real guard, with no hand-computed comparisons. Re-judged from the owner's own words: the chained over-replication follows from the DELIBERATE drain-phase invisibility (move-planner-state-methods.js:349-357), so it is required-for-availability, while the budget reliance stays accidental because no module authorizes the promotion and the ordinary hand-off needs no budget. The ledger's lab line is re-explained truthfully as a chained relocation during the first one's drain on three co-located voters; the census disagreement does NOT explain it and the round-1 claim that it did was wrong. B3: the pinned grant rule is now outcome honoured AND wouldBeWithinAuthorizedBound; a record authorizing five evaluated for a promotion to eight is honoured and is refused only by the conjunction. Cases above and below the bound were added, every refusal reason the owner defines is in the case set (intent-unknown through a hand-built binding), and thirteen wrong rules die. B4: the expand and paired-relocation rows are does_not_depend and still-unclassified with what would classify them, and the ledger row is split into seven producer rows mirroring the five. B5: the census is data-flow aware to a fixed point - seed 127 tokens, 3 rounds, 23 aliases discovered including all 14 the verifier's probe found, plus the carrier's own tokens - 150 tokens over 1207 sites; three misclassified entries are now projections; every entry answers what it observes or says unknown_not_traced; the blind spots are in the limits. B6: the validator is structural and all nine of the verifier's mutations are CAUGHT on a green baseline. B7: every gate status is derived by one shared function from the rows, the open findings and the declared owner decisions, and comes out 1 not-yet, 2 not-yet, 3 blocked, 4 not-yet, 5 blocked, 6 blocked, 7 not-yet, 8 demonstrated, 9 not-yet. The lead's three rulings are recorded. The landed host test file learner-promotion-count-check-inputs.test.js is restored byte-identical to HEAD; the unmintable-partition receipt now has its own file whose grid IS the domain the proved-unreachable rows state (1,360,800 states, 12 s).

round 2 REJECT (5 blocking, narrower than round 1; judged exactly as submitted). Repaired and upheld: the two missing rows exist and assert the real retention owner; the REPLACE premise is corrected and driven on real owners; the pinned grant rule is the safe conjunction; the unreachable grid drives the real methods, completion owner and count check over 45 x 30240 states with ranges equal to the domain object; all nine round-1 mutations caught; census limits disclosed; the lead's receipt-2 restatement is sound (the sealed quest carries receipt ids only) - an independent class map finds 16 classes, all inside the matrix's 20. R2-1 the chained-REPLACE classification 'required-for-availability' inverts the owner's words: move-planner-move-calculation-methods.js:671-688 SERIALIZES REPLACE on critical partitions to one in flight because more 'only builds a mutual-defer standoff'; driven on the real follow-up builder, four ACTIVE voters give over_replication_suppressed and only a prior target still SYNCING in a voter role yields a second REPLACE, so the producer chains only through the census disagreement the matrix says does not explain it; the end-to-end test drives the builder at target and then hands the guard a hand-built four-voter membership (stitched); in the lab REPLACE #1 was settled by the recovery drain (owner_unavailable_released, source removal_required) 2.4 s before REPLACE #2 was dispatched - an operation settled with its source still present - and no line names #2's producer, so the attribution is INFERRED. R2-2 does_not_depend has no structural proof: flipping a depends row or the lab-witnessed minted row to does_not_depend stays green; two ledger rows carry does_not_depend together with budgetRemovalChangesTheDecision true; no test drives the paired-relocation producer, which R2-1 makes a live candidate for the lab's chained REPLACE. R2-3 gate statuses are derived from hand-declared inputs the validator does not pin: emptying an item's openFindings, dropping its requires or pointing it at one classified row turns it demonstrated; item 8 has no requires and no rows and can only ever be demonstrated. R2-4 wrong grant rules survive: an off-by-one bound (no case at authorized+1), 'within !== false' (no case with an unreadable promotion count, for which the landed evaluation returns honoured true with within null), and a rule skipping the bound below 5. R2-5 gate item 5 still asserts completeness; a fourth blind spot is undisclosed - renames into names that do not spell epoch (source_snapshot_version, publicationRevision, desiredPublicationRevision, stamp): 7 tokens at 13 sites; 74 INFERRED entries carry generic non-answers while the limits say they answer unknown_not_traced. Findings against the owner's decisions of 2026-09-19 night (corrections, not reject reasons): Decision 2 CONFIRMED from code - the follow-up move decides the same distinct-node spread condition the cure policy classifies for ADD, a split owner, so priority_recovery_relocation is not warranted and the scope becomes 'unify the decision owner across mechanisms' (replacement_handoff_overlap needs the same test); Decision 4 - the establishing-window and undeclared-row rows are still-unclassified and their scopes dropped (the undeclared case depends on the budget only when the planner's and the learner's caches disagree, since the guard's own target falls to 0 on an unreadable row); Decision 3 - no ledger-local reason is shown (the local need is a +1 relocation the replacement allowance covers; the second voter comes from the chain), so the ledger relocation row is still-unclassified; Decision 1 - item 8 is not-yet and the inherited test must become outcome === honoured alone with NOT-honoured cases for bound+1, malformed and absent bound, unreadable count, wrong partition, wrong authority, future, invalid and zero epoch. Gate: 1,2,4,7,8,9 not-yet; 3,5,6 blocked on the owner. Statics and all quest tests green; no production or landed file touched.

Round-3 rework against the verifier's five blocking findings and the owner's eleven binding rules; all twelve receipts green, probe metric 0, and the matrix rebuilt from 25 to 27 rows. R2-1 (chained REPLACE): the round-2 classification required-for-availability is WITHDRAWN and recorded as correctionToRound2 - it inverted the owner's words, who caps concurrent REPLACE on critical partitions at one in flight because more "only builds a mutual-defer standoff" (move-planner-move-calculation-methods.js:671-688). The admission class is now SPLIT per the owner's rule 1 into an ordinary promote-then-remove hand-off overlap (does_not_depend, measured over the complete stated domain) and a view-disagreement overlap (depends, still-unclassified, carrying the owner's requirement verbatim). The witness is ONE drive: real builder -> real coordinator -> durable replica_operations row -> real guard, with the learner identity taken from the row the coordinator wrote rather than hand-built; it shows ACTIVE prior target => over_replication_suppressed and SYNCING prior target => a second REPLACE, so the census disagreement is the only way the chain is reached. Lab attribution is INFERRED/owner_unavailable_released and reads the unattributed sentence. R2-2: dependency is now a five-value enum, each value owing a structural receipt the validator enforces; the paired relocation is unknown_producer_not_driven. R2-3: the gate's whole contract (selection, minimums, requirements, blocking decisions, blocking findings, required external artifacts) moved beside the derivation, rows are SELECTED not listed, and six monotonicity mutants prove no deletion can demonstrate an item; item 8 is not-yet behind a required external artifact that does not exist. R2-4: bound cases at, above, below, unreadable, missing, zero and very small, with V1-V3 mutants, and the inherited requirement recorded verbatim. R2-5: the inventory groups its 150 tokens three ways (44 traced, 66 rule-classified, 8 data-flow aliases, 32 unresolved) and the validator rejects any completeness claim. Findings carry gateItems and an open flag; repair quests are grouped by semantic cause with no ledger-authority quest; three architectural results are recorded, not encoded. Production untouched; nothing started.

round 3 REJECT (3 blocking, all ORDINARY defects, so the owner's stopping condition is met - no attempt 4 at this altitude). The content is sound: 25 of 27 rows upheld as written, all nine gate statuses agreed, the chained REPLACE is genuinely one real drive (ACTIVE prior target suppressed, SYNCING prior target yields a second REPLACE, granted with the budget and refused at zero), producer-reachable is yes on only five rows all citing real-chain files, lab attribution is either the uniquely attributable minted payload or the unattributed sentence, counts per machine, the six owner monotonicity mutants and the verifier's earlier N3-N6 and N10 are caught, V1-V3 and two new wrong grant rules die, all seven epoch-less renames are now inventoried (44 traced, 66 rule-classified, 8 data-flow aliases, 32 unresolved), no conflict with an owner decision beyond the ledger row below, statics and all quest tests green, no production or landed file touched. D1 non-structural validator: item 8 can be made demonstrated by setting the finding honoured-does-not-include-the-bound to open false, unlinking it and setting the required external artifact's hand-written exists flag true; a finding's open flag needs no resolution receipt, so items 6 and 7 can be demonstrated the same way. D2 non-structural validator: the rule-4 and rule-2 receipts are pointers not bound to the row - a depends row flipped to does_not_depend citing an unrelated existing test stays green, and any row may claim producerReachable yes by citing a file that declares itself real-chain without driving that row's producer. D3 incorrect classification: five-relocation-handoff-overlap and ledger-relocation-handoff-overlap carry does_not_depend (measured soundly on the real guard over the complete hand-off class: no state changes when the budget is zeroed) together with explicit-authority-required; removing the budget changes nothing for this class, so no authority has to replace it, the ledger row conflicts with the owner's rule that the ordinary +1 is covered by the replacement allowance and that no ledger authority is proposed, and gate item 3's row selection inherits the error; the fitting disposition is proved-unreachable within the hand-off domain, with the spread-recovery-owner unification kept as a finding. Architectural results judged: producer identity is not guard-visible (genuine impossibility); the released nodes' lab attribution is unrecoverable from the recorded logs (genuine limit); the epoch domain cannot be closed by a spelling census (a true limit of method, correctly left to the domain-closing quest). Non-blocking: a lexical validator cannot close 'equivalents' of completeness nor detect a timing attribution mislabelled as a trace; matrix and gate notes are not scanned for completeness words; two test headers overclaim 'nothing hand-built' (status and workflow_step are overwritten and the learner service row is hand-made - shown immaterial: the unmodified coordinator row gives the same result); one wrong citation in an architectural result. Freeze judgment: not byte-for-byte; D3 is the only correction the CONTENT needs, D1 and D2 affect later edits, not the submitted values.

Round 3 rejected on three ordinary defects (D1 hand-written finding and external-artifact truth, D2 receipts not bound to the row they prove, D3 two hand-off rows carrying does_not_depend together with explicit-authority-required), which meets the owner's stopping condition: no attempt 4 at this altitude. The content stands as inherited evidence - 25 of 27 rows upheld, all nine gate statuses agreed, three architectural results judged genuine. The narrow successor corrects D3, binds the evidence, and freezes the matrix and gate document on independent approval; this quest's matrix, inventory, gate document and tests move to it unfrozen.
